text: There was a man from Benjamin whose name was Kish son of Abiel, son of Zeror, son of Becorath, son of Aphiah, son of a Benjaminite; he was a man of standing.

versions.text: There was a man from Benjamin whose name was Kish son of Abiel, son of Zeror, son of Becorath, son of Aphiah, a Benjaminite, a man of substance.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew continues the genealogical chain with בֶּן־אִישׁ יְמִינִי, "son of a Benjaminite man." As it stands, the chain is broken and "a Benjaminite" simply repeats the opening phrase. Separating the closing description into its own clause also reads more smoothly aloud.

text: He had a son named Saul, young and handsome. There was no one among the Israelites more handsome than he; he stood head and shoulders above all the people.
Now the donkeys belonging to Kish, Saul's father, had strayed off, and Kish said to his son Saul, "Take one of the servants with you and go look for the donkeys."

So he passed through the hill country of Ephraim and through the region of Shalishah, but they did not find them. They went on through the region of Shaalim, and they were not there. They passed through the territory of Benjamin, and still did not find them.
When they came to the region of Zuph, Saul said to the servant who was with him, "Come, let us go back, or my father will stop worrying about the donkeys and start worrying about us."
But the servant said to him, "Listen, there is a man of God in this town, and he is highly respected; everything he says comes true. Let us go there now. Perhaps he will tell us which way to take."
Saul said to his servant, "If we go, what can we bring the man? The bread in our bags is gone, and we have no gift to bring the man of God. What do we have?"
The servant answered Saul again, "Look, I have a quarter shekel of silver here. I will give it to the man of God, and he will tell us our way."
(Formerly in Israel, when a man went to inquire of God, he would say, "Come, let us go to the seer," for the one now called a prophet was formerly called a seer.)
Saul said to his servant, "Well said. Come, let us go." So they set out for the town where the man of God was.

versions.text: Saul said to his servant, "Good idea. Come, let us go." So they set out for the town where the man of God was.
versions.explanation: טוֹב דְּבָרְךָ literally "your word is good"; "Well said" keeps closer to the idiom and avoids the modern colloquial tone of "Good idea" while remaining natural for oral reading.

text: As they were climbing the hill to the town, they met some young women coming out to draw water and asked them, "Is the seer here?"
"He is," they answered. "He is just ahead of you. Hurry now, for he has come to town today, since the people have a sacrifice at the high place.

As soon as you enter the town you will find him, before he goes up to the high place to eat. The people will not eat until he comes, because he must bless the sacrifice; only then will the guests eat. Go up now, for you will find him today.

versions.text: As soon as you enter the town you will find him, before he goes up to the high place to eat. The people will not eat until he comes, because he must bless the sacrifice; only then will the guests eat. Go up now, for you will find him at once."
versions.explanation: כְהַיּוֹם means "today" / "this very day," echoing the earlier "today" of verse 12. "At once" drops the temporal marker that ties the girls' answer together.

text: So they went up to the town. As they were entering it, there was Samuel, coming toward them on his way up to the high place.
Now the day before Saul came, the LORD had revealed this to Samuel:

"About this time tomorrow I will send you a man from the land of Benjamin. Anoint him ruler over my people Israel; he will deliver my people from the hand of the Philistines. For I have looked upon my people, because their cry has come to me."
When Samuel caught sight of Saul, the LORD said to him, "Here is the man I spoke to you about; this one will govern my people."
Saul approached Samuel in the gateway and said, "Tell me, please, where is the seer's house?"
"I am the seer," Samuel answered. "Go up ahead of me to the high place, for today you are to eat with me. In the morning I will send you on your way and tell you all that is on your mind.
As for the donkeys you lost three days ago, do not give them another thought; they have been found. And to whom does all that Israel desires belong, if not to you and to all your father's house?"
Saul answered, "Am I not a Benjaminite, from the smallest of the tribes of Israel, and is not my clan the least of all the clans of the tribe of Benjamin? Why do you speak to me like this?"
Then Samuel took Saul and his servant, brought them into the hall, and seated them at the head of the guests, who numbered about thirty.
Samuel said to the cook, "Bring the portion I gave you, the one I told you to set aside."

So the cook took up the thigh with what was on it and set it before Saul. Samuel said, "Here is what was kept back. Set it before you and eat, for it was reserved for you for this occasion, when I said, 'I have invited the people.'" And Saul ate with Samuel that day.
After they came down from the high place into the town, Samuel talked with Saul on the roof.
They rose early, and at daybreak Samuel called up to Saul on the roof, "Get ready, and I will send you on your way." Saul got up, and the two of them, he and Samuel, went outside together.

As they were going down to the edge of the town, Samuel said to Saul, "Tell the servant to go on ahead of us"—and he went on—"but you stay here a moment, so that I may make known to you the word of God."
